blocks.text: The query results list six individuals in the EMEA region who have Python proficiency at level 4 or higher and are less than 60% hard-booked between March and May 2026. Their hard-booked hours range from 0 to 26 hours out of a total capacity of 520 hours in that period, resulting in hard-booked percentages from 0% up to 5%. The individuals are Anthony Thompson, Kevin Robinson, Edward Hill, Matthew Hill, Matthew White, and David Allen. The data is complete for this query and no truncation occurred.

blocks.title: List people in EMEA with Python skill proficiency >=4 and hard-booked less than 60% between March and May 2026, including person_id, name, hard_booked_hours and hard_booked_pct.

blocks.purpose: List people in EMEA with Python skill proficiency >=4 and hard-booked less than 60% between March and May 2026, including person_id, name, hard_booked_hours and hard_booked_pct.
blocks.sql:
WITH skill_python AS (
    SELECT ps.person_id
    FROM person_skills ps
    JOIN skills s ON ps.skill_id = s.skill_id
    WHERE s.name = 'Python' AND ps.proficiency >= 4
),
booked_hours AS (
    SELECT
        b.person_id,
        SUM(b.minutes) / 60.0 AS hard_booked_hours
    FROM bookings b
    WHERE b.kind = 'hard'
      AND b.start_ts < :window_end
      AND b.end_ts > :window_start
    GROUP BY b.person_id
),
people_emea AS (
    SELECT p.person_id, p.display_name
    FROM people p
    WHERE p.location_region = 'EMEA'
),
capacity AS (
    SELECT :capacity_hours AS capacity_hours
)
SELECT
    p.person_id,
    p.display_name AS name,
    COALESCE(bh.hard_booked_hours, 0) AS hard_booked_hours,
    CASE WHEN c.capacity_hours > 0 THEN (COALESCE(bh.hard_booked_hours, 0) / c.capacity_hours) * 100 ELSE NULL END AS hard_booked_pct
FROM people_emea p
JOIN skill_python sp ON p.person_id = sp.person_id
LEFT JOIN booked_hours bh ON p.person_id = bh.person_id
CROSS JOIN capacity c
WHERE (COALESCE(bh.hard_booked_hours, 0) / c.capacity_hours) * 100 < 60
ORDER BY p.person_id ASC;

assumptions: The date range March to May 2026 is inclusive, so start_date is 2026-03-01 and end_date is 2026-05-31.
Hard-booked means bookings with kind='hard' including completed rows, counting minutes intersecting the date range, converted to hours.
Proficiency 4 or higher means person_skills with skill='Python' and proficiency >= 4.
Region EMEA means people.location_region = 'EMEA'.
Less than 60% hard-booked means total hard booking hours in the date range divided by total available hours in that range is less than 0.6.

These requirements have an open status (status_id in the open state group) and their requirement_id is not found in the set of submitted requests. The table includes details such as requirement_id, name, engagement_id, role_category_id, status_id, work location, effort, duration, remaining duration, fulfilled duration, fulfilled hours, percentage filled, cost price in cents, quantity, city, state or province, country, latitude, longitude, request status, and timestamps for creation and update. blocks.title: List all open resource requirements belonging to engagements with a critical risk and no submitted request

blocks.purpose: List all open resource requirements belonging to engagements with a critical risk and no submitted request
blocks.sql:
WITH critical_engagements AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT engagement_id
    FROM risks
    WHERE severity = 'critical'
), open_requirements AS (
    SELECT rr.requirement_id
    FROM requirement_requests rr
    WHERE rr.state = 'submitted'
), open_resource_requirements AS (
    SELECT rr.*
    FROM resource_requirements rr
    JOIN status_lookup sl ON rr.status_id = sl.status_id
    WHERE sl.domain = 'requirement' AND sl.state_group = 'open'
)
SELECT orr.*
FROM open_resource_requirements orr
JOIN critical_engagements ce ON orr.engagement_id = ce.engagement_id
WHERE orr.requirement_id NOT IN (SELECT requirement_id FROM open_requirements)
ORDER BY orr.requirement_id ASC;

assumptions: Open resource requirements are those with status_id in the open state group for requirements.
Engagements with a critical risk have at least one risk record with severity='critical'.
No submitted request means there is no requirement_requests record with state='submitted' for the requirement.

blocks.text: The total planned cost of active engagements in the Healthcare & Life Sciences (HLS) business unit, converted to the reporting currency (primary currency), is $5,157,842.10. This total is derived by summing the planned costs (originally in cents) of engagements with active status (status code 'ACT' in the 'project' domain) within the HLS business unit, converting each to the reporting currency using the latest foreign exchange rates. There are 11 such active engagements included in this total. The calculation assumes the primary currency is identified by the 'is_primary' flag in the currencies table, and the HLS business unit is identified by the code 'HLS'. The provided result is complete and not truncated.

blocks.title: Calculate total planned cost in reporting currency and count of active engagements in Healthcare & Life Sciences business unit

blocks.purpose: Calculate total planned cost in reporting currency and count of active engagements in Healthcare & Life Sciences business unit
blocks.sql:
WITH primary_currency AS (
    SELECT currency_id
    FROM currencies
    WHERE is_primary = 1
    LIMIT 1
), fx_rates AS (
    SELECT currency_id, MAX(fx_rate) AS fx_rate
    FROM rate_cards
    GROUP BY currency_id
), hls_bu AS (
    SELECT business_unit_id
    FROM business_units
    WHERE code = 'HLS'
    LIMIT 1
), active_status AS (
    SELECT status_id
    FROM status_lookup
    WHERE domain = 'project' AND code = 'ACT'
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
    ROUND(SUM(CAST(e.planned_cost_cents AS REAL) / 100.0 * fr.fx_rate), 2) AS total_usd,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.engagement_id) AS engagement_count
FROM engagements e
JOIN hls_bu bu ON e.business_unit_id = bu.business_unit_id
JOIN active_status s ON e.status_id = s.status_id
JOIN primary_currency pc ON 1=1
LEFT JOIN fx_rates fr ON e.currency_id = fr.currency_id
WHERE e.planned_cost_cents IS NOT NULL;

assumptions: Active engagements are those with status_lookup domain='project' and code='ACT'.
The reporting currency is identified by currencies.is_primary=1.
Planned cost is taken from engagements.planned_cost_cents converted to reporting currency using rate_cards.fx_rate.
The Healthcare & Life Sciences business unit corresponds to business_units.code='HLS'.

blocks.title: Count people in each region with DSPy / LLM Ops skill at proficiency 3 or higher

blocks.purpose: Count people in each region with DSPy / LLM Ops skill at proficiency 3 or higher
blocks.sql:
WITH dspy_skill AS (
  SELECT skill_id FROM skills WHERE name = 'DSPy / LLM Ops'
), qualified_people AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ps.person_id
  FROM person_skills ps
  JOIN dspy_skill ds ON ps.skill_id = ds.skill_id
  WHERE ps.proficiency >= 3
)
SELECT p.location_region AS region, COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) AS people
FROM people p
JOIN qualified_people qp ON p.person_id = qp.person_id
GROUP BY p.location_region
ORDER BY p.location_region ASC;

assumptions: Proficiency 3 or higher means proficiency >= 3.
Regions are as per people.location_region field with values like AMER, APAC, EMEA, LATAM.

WITH engagement_work_items AS (

filtered_time_entries AS (

GROUP BY p.person_id, p.display_name

LIMIT 5;

blocks.purpose: Count total number of blocked critical-path work items on active engagements
blocks.sql:
WITH active_engagements AS (
  SELECT engagement_id
  FROM engagements
  WHERE status_id = (SELECT status_id FROM status_lookup WHERE domain = 'project' AND code = 'ACT' LIMIT 1)
), blocked_critical_items AS (
  SELECT wi.work_item_id
  FROM work_items wi
  JOIN status_lookup sl ON wi.status_id = sl.status_id
  WHERE wi.is_critical = 1
    AND sl.domain = 'task' AND sl.code = 'BLK'
    AND wi.engagement_id IN (SELECT engagement_id FROM active_engagements)
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT work_item_id) AS total_blocked_critical_items
FROM blocked_critical_items;

blocks.purpose: Top 5 active engagements ranked by number of blocked critical-path work items
blocks.sql:
WITH active_engagements AS (
  SELECT engagement_id, code
  FROM engagements
  WHERE status_id = (SELECT status_id FROM status_lookup WHERE domain = 'project' AND code = 'ACT' LIMIT 1)
), blocked_critical_items AS (
  SELECT wi.work_item_id, wi.engagement_id
  FROM work_items wi
  JOIN status_lookup sl ON wi.status_id = sl.status_id
  WHERE wi.is_critical = 1
    AND sl.domain = 'task' AND sl.code = 'BLK'
    AND wi.engagement_id IN (SELECT engagement_id FROM active_engagements)
)
SELECT ae.engagement_id, ae.code AS engagement_code, COUNT(bci.work_item_id) AS blocked_critical_items
FROM active_engagements ae
LEFT JOIN blocked_critical_items bci ON ae.engagement_id = bci.engagement_id
GROUP BY ae.engagement_id, ae.code
ORDER BY blocked_critical_items DESC
LIMIT 5;

assumptions: Active engagements are those with status code 'ACT' in the project domain as of reference date 2026-04-01.
Blocked work items have status code 'BLK' in the task domain.
Critical-path work items are those with is_critical=1.

According to the provided SQL query and its results, there are 11 such people. The assumptions clarify that proficiency 4 or higher means proficiency >= 4, the region APAC is identified by people.location_region = 'APAC', and the skill name is exactly 'Python'. The result is not truncated and is based on the exact data from the source tables people, person_skills, and skills.

blocks.title: Count of people in APAC region with Python skill proficiency 4 or higher

blocks.purpose: Count of people in APAC region with Python skill proficiency 4 or higher
blocks.sql:
WITH python_skill AS (
  SELECT skill_id FROM skills WHERE name = 'Python'
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) AS people
FROM people p
JOIN person_skills ps ON p.person_id = ps.person_id
JOIN python_skill sk ON ps.skill_id = sk.skill_id
WHERE p.location_region = 'APAC'
  AND ps.proficiency >= 4;

assumptions: Proficiency 4 or higher means proficiency >= 4.
Region APAC corresponds to people.location_region = 'APAC'.
Skill name is exactly 'Python'.
Count distinct people meeting these criteria.

blocks.title: Find people who have Python, Ruby on Rails, and PostgreSQL all at proficiency 5

blocks.purpose: Find people who have Python, Ruby on Rails, and PostgreSQL all at proficiency 5
blocks.sql:
WITH skill_ids AS (
  SELECT skill_id, name FROM skills WHERE name IN ('Python', 'Ruby on Rails', 'PostgreSQL')
), person_skill_counts AS (
  SELECT ps.person_id
  FROM person_skills ps
  JOIN skill_ids s ON ps.skill_id = s.skill_id
  WHERE ps.proficiency = 5
  GROUP BY ps.person_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ps.skill_id) = 3
)
SELECT p.person_id, p.display_name
FROM people p
JOIN person_skill_counts psc ON p.person_id = psc.person_id
ORDER BY p.display_name ASC;

This amount is calculated by summing the amounts in billing_documents where the currency is BRL, converting these amounts from cents to the base unit, and then applying the latest available foreign exchange rate (fx_rate) from the rate_cards table to convert BRL to USD. The calculation uses the maximum fx_rate per currency to ensure the most recent rate is applied. Only vendor invoices denominated in BRL are included in this total. The result is rounded to two decimal places and represents the aggregate USD value of all such invoices.

blocks.title: Calculate total value in USD of vendor invoices issued in BRL currency

blocks.purpose: Calculate total value in USD of vendor invoices issued in BRL currency
blocks.sql: WITH fx AS (SELECT currency_id, MAX(fx_rate) AS fx_rate FROM rate_cards GROUP BY currency_id), brl_currency AS (SELECT currency_id FROM currencies WHERE iso_code = 'BRL') SELECT ROUND(SUM(bd.amount_cents * fx.fx_rate) / 100.0, 2) AS total_usd_value FROM billing_documents bd JOIN brl_currency brl ON bd.currency_id = brl.currency_id JOIN fx ON bd.currency_id = fx.currency_id;

assumptions: The total value is the sum of billing_documents amounts where currency is BRL, converted to USD using the latest available fx_rate from rate_cards.
Use the fx_rate from rate_cards to convert BRL amounts to the reporting currency USD, not assuming rate=1.
Only vendor invoices (billing_documents) are considered, filtered by currency_id corresponding to BRL.

blocks.text: Person ID 348 has a total of 30.0 hard-booked hours across all booking periods. This total is calculated by summing all bookings with kind='hard' for this person and converting the total minutes to hours by dividing by 60. The data includes all booking statuses and covers all time periods without any truncation or filtering.

blocks.title: Calculate total hard-booked hours for person ID 348 across all booking periods

blocks.purpose: Calculate total hard-booked hours for person ID 348 across all booking periods
blocks.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CAST(bookings.minutes AS REAL)) / 60.0, 0) AS hard_booked_hours
FROM bookings
WHERE bookings.person_id = :person_id
  AND bookings.kind = 'hard';

assumptions: Sum all bookings with kind='hard' for person ID 348 across all time periods.
Convert booking minutes to hours by dividing by 60.
Include all booking statuses, including completed ones.
